p0.original: 第十章 充分表达愤怒

p1.original: 关于如何表达愤怒，非暴力沟通和其他沟通方式有着显著的区别。通过探讨非暴力沟通表达愤怒的过程，我们可以更深入地了解非暴力沟通。
p1.en: There is a marked difference between Nonviolent Communication and other forms of communication on how to express anger. By exploring the process of expressing anger through Nonviolent Communication, we can learn more about Nonviolent Communication.

p2.original: 我想说的是，杀人太肤浅了。在生气时，杀人、打人、骂人都无法真正传达我们的心声。如果真的很生气，我们就需要找到强有力的方式充分表达自己。
p2.en: What I'm trying to say is that killing is too superficial. Killing, beating and scolding do not really convey our voices when they are angry. If we are really angry, we need to find a strong way to fully express ourselves.

p3.original: 听到这样的观点，许多人松了一口气。他们受到了压迫和歧视，生活痛苦不堪。“不要生气”“接受现实”之类的话，他们已经听得太多了。那些话听起来就像是在教训他们。他们没有兴趣再听一些高谈阔论，而想学一些实用的知识，来减轻痛苦。幸运的是，非暴力沟通并不主张忽视或压抑愤怒，它认为，通过深入地了解愤怒，我们可以充分表达内心的渴望。
p3.en: Many people are relieved to hear that. They suffer from oppression and discrimination. They've heard too much about the words “crazy” and “accept reality”. That sounds like a lesson to them. They are not interested in listening to more talk, but rather in learning practical knowledge to alleviate their suffering. Fortunately, Nonviolent Communication does not advocate neglect or repression of anger, and it is argued that by in-depth knowledge of anger, we can fully express our internal aspirations.

p5.original: 充分表达愤怒的第一步是我们不再归咎于他人。如果我们认为“他让我很生气”，那么，我们难免就会指责他人。然而，实际情况是，我们心情并不取决于他人的行为。
p5.en: The first step in fully expressing our anger is that we no longer blame others. If we think that “he makes me angry”, then we will inevitably blame others. The reality, however, is that our mood does not depend on the behaviour of others.

p6.original: 我想举一个例子来说明外在刺激与内在原因之间的区别。在瑞士的监狱，我曾给那里的囚犯讲解如何表达愤怒，而不是去杀人、打人或强暴妇女。其中有个练习是请他们写下某件激怒他们的事情。一位名叫约翰的犯人写道：“三个星期前，我向监狱的官员提出了一个请求，至今他们仍没有反馈。”很明显，他写下了他的观察。
p6.en: I would like to give an example of the difference between external incentives and underlying causes. In the Swiss prison, I told the prisoners there how to express their anger rather than killing, beating or raping women. One of the exercises was to ask them to write something that angered them. A prisoner named John wrote: “Three weeks ago, I made a request to the prison officials, and they have not yet received a response. Apparently, he wrote down his observations.

p7.original: 接着，我请他解释他生气的原因：“发生这个事情后，为什么你会生气呢？”
p7.en: Then I asked him to explain why he was angry: "Why are you angry after this?"

p8.original: “我刚才已经和你说了，”他大声地说道，“我生气是因为他们没有回应我的请求。”看来，他把外在刺激等同于内在原因，并认为监狱官员的行为让他生气。如果在一个社会中，内疚被运用来控制人；那么，指责他人就容易成为一种习惯。同时，为了使这种手段奏效，我们可能就会认为一个人可以主导另一个人的情绪。
p8.en: “I told you earlier,” he said aloud, “I am angry because they did not respond to my request. It appears that he equates external stimulation with underlying causes and believes that the behaviour of prison officials makes him angry. If guilt is used to control people in a society; Then it is easy to blame others. At the same time, in order for such a tool to work, we may think that one person can dominate the emotions of another.

p9.original: 在前面的章节中，我们提到，“你成绩不好让爸爸妈妈伤透了心！”这样的话是希望孩子们相信，他们的行为造成了父母的痛苦。同样的，情人之间也可能会说：“你没来庆祝我的生日，让我很失望。”类似的话还有，“你要气死我啊”“你那样做让我很难过”“你真给我丢脸”等等。
p9.en: In the previous section, we said, "You're not doing well to break Mom and Dad! That is to hope that the children will believe that their actions have caused the suffering of their parents. Likewise, lovers might say, "You didn't come to celebrate my birthday, and I'm disappointed. And like, "You have to be mad at me," "You've made me feel bad about that," "You've really embarrassed me," etc.

p10.original: 到底是什么让我们生气呢？我们从第五章了解到，听到不中听的话时，我们有四种选择：1.责备自己；2.指责他人；3.体会自己的感受和需要；4.体会他人的感受和需要。当我们选择第二种反应时，我们认为别人应当认错或受罚——我相信这就是我们生气的原因。
p10.en: What the hell is making us angry? From chapter V, we understand that when we hear things, we have four options: 1. To blame ourselves; 2. Stigmatizing others; 3. To appreciate their own feelings and needs; To appreciate the feelings and needs of others. When we choose the second response, we believe that others should be mistaken or punished — and I believe that is why we are angry.

p11.original: 当我们选择第三种反应时，我们专注于自己的感受和需要。我们用心体会着自己，而不再分析别人犯了什么错。我们越是用心体会自己的感受和需要，我们也就越能留意到自己的心理活动。
p11.en: When we choose the third response, we focus on our own feelings and needs. We know ourselves with our hearts, and we don't analyse what others have done. The more we feel our feelings and needs, the more we are aware of our psychological activities.

p12.original: 假定我们约了个人，时间到了，她却没来。如果彼此的关系处于比较微妙的时期，我们可能会忧心忡忡。如果我们看重的是诚实守信，我们也许会觉得不耐烦。反之，如果我们想休息一会儿，我们可能就不会介意她来晚了。因此，同一件事情，不同的需要导致不同的感受。一旦意识到自己的需要——不论是友谊、诚信还是休息，我们就可以更加体贴自己。我们可能会有强烈的情绪，但不再生气。可是，如果意识不到自己尚未满足的需要，一心考虑别人的过错，我们难免就会生气。
p12.en: Assuming we had a date, time was up, and she didn't come. We may be worried if our relationship is at a delicate time. We may find impatience if we value honesty. On the contrary, if we wanted to take a break, we wouldn't mind her coming late. Thus, the same thing, different needs lead to different feelings. Once we realize our needs — be it friendship, honesty or rest — we can be more sensitive to ourselves. We may have a strong mood, but no longer angry. But if we are not aware of the needs we have yet to meet and are concerned about the faults of others, we will inevitably get angry.

p13.original: 除了专注于自身的感受和需要，我们还可以选择去体会对方的感受和需要。此时，我们也不会感到生气。我们无须压抑愤怒，只要我们专注于他人的感受和需要，愤怒也就不再存在。
p13.en: In addition to focusing on our own feelings and needs, we can choose to appreciate each other's feelings and needs. We will not be angry at this moment. We do not have to suppress anger, and it will no longer exist as long as we focus on the feelings and needs of others.

p15.original: “但是，”有人问我，“在有些情况下，愤怒不是理所当然的吗？例如，看到各种破坏环境的行为，愤怒不正是正直的表现吗？”我的回答是，如果我把人看作是“正直的”或“不正直的”，“负责任的”或“不负责任的”，那么，我的想法也会带来暴力。我坚信，专注于我们的需要，比评判他人是什么人，更有益于生活。
p15.en: “But,” I was asked, “In some cases, is anger not natural? For example, isn't anger a manifestation of integrity when it comes to seeing all kinds of environmental damage? My answer is that if I see people as “improbable” or “improper”, “responsible” or “irresponsibility”, then my thoughts also lead to violence. I firmly believe that it is better to focus on our needs than to judge who others are.

p16.original: 在我看来，愤怒是我们的思维方式造成的。它的核心是尚未满足的需要。如果我们能够借助它来提醒自己——我们有需要没有得到满足，而我们的思维方式正使它难以得到满足，那愤怒就是有价值的。为了充分表达愤怒，我们有必要明了自己的需要并采取行动。然而，做到这一点并不容易。因为愤怒驱使我们去惩罚他人，而不是去满足需要。为此，我建议，与其沉浸于“合理的愤怒”，不如倾听自己和他人的需要。这也许需要一个过程，但通过不断的实践，我们将会有意识地用“我生气是因为我需要……”来取代“我生气是因为他们……”。
p16.en: In my view, anger is the result of our way of thinking. At the heart of it is the unmet need. If we can use it to remind ourselves that we have needs that are not being met and that our way of thinking is making them difficult to meet, then anger is worth it. In order to fully express our anger, we need to understand our needs and act. However, this is not easy. Because anger drives us to punish others, not to satisfy needs. For this reason, I suggest that instead of being immersed in “reasonable anger”, we listen to ourselves and others' needs. This may require a process, but through continuous practice, we will consciously replace “I am angry because I need to be angry because they” with “I am angry because they ”.

p17.original: 我曾在威斯康星州的一所学校提供咨询服务。连续两天，在劝架时，我的鼻子都挨了重重一击。第一天，我的鼻子被一个孩子的肘部击中了。我差点就一拳打了回去。在我小时候，只要受了轻微的伤害，我都会给予回击。第二天，又有两个小孩吵架，我的鼻子被一个小孩打中了，这次痛得更厉害，血流得更多，但我并没有生气。
p17.en: I've been consulting at a school in Wisconsin. For two days in a row, my nose was hit in the middle of a fight. On the first day, my nose was hit by a child's elbow. I almost punched back. When I was a kid, I'd give back a little bit of a blow. The next day, two more children fought, and I was hit in the nose by a child, and this time it hurts worse and bleeds more, but I'm not angry.

p18.original: 当我回想起那两天的经历时，我发现，我一开始就把第一个孩子看作是“被宠坏的孩子”。所以，他打到我时，我极为恼怒。我心里想：“这家伙太猖狂了！”我对第二个孩子的看法则不同，我把他看作是“软弱的孩子”。由于我比较担心这个孩子，当我的鼻子被他打伤时，我并没有责怪他。这段经历帮助我认识到，我生气的原因不在于别人做了什么，而在于我怎么看待对方及其行为。
p18.en: When I remembered those two days, I found out that I had seen my first child as a “smuggled child” from the beginning. So when he hit me, I was very angry. I thought, "This guy is crazy! “I see the second child differently, and I see him as a “weak child”. Because I'm worried about this kid, I didn't blame him when he hurt my nose. This experience helped me to realize that I was angry not because of what others did, but because of how I saw the other side and its behaviour.

p20.original: 下文是我在瑞士监狱中与约翰的谈话记录。我想借助它来说明区分外在刺激与内在原因的实际意义。
p20.en: The following is a record of my conversation with John in a Swiss prison. I would like to use it to illustrate the practical significance of distinguishing between external incentives and underlying causes.

p21.original: 约 翰：“三个星期前，我向监狱的官员提出了一个请求，至今他们仍没有反馈。”
p21.en: Johan: “Three weeks ago, I sent a request to prison officials, who have still not received feedback.

p22.original: 马歇尔：“发生这个事情后，为什么你会生气呢？”
p22.en: Marshall, "Why are you angry after this?"

p23.original: 约 翰：“我刚才已经和你说了，我生气是因为他们没有回应我的请求。”
p23.en: Johan: I've just told you, I'm angry because they didn't respond to my request.

p24.original: 马歇尔：“等一下。在你说‘我生气是因为他们……’时，停下来想一想，你和自己说是什么让你生气了？”
p24.en: Marshall: Wait a minute. When you say, "I'm angry because of them...", stop and think, what do you say to yourself that makes you angry?

p25.original: 约 翰：“我没和自己说什么。”
p25.en: Johan: I didn't say anything to myself.

p26.original: 马歇尔：“好，现在停下来，好好体会一下你的心情和想法。”
p26.en: Marshall: "Well, stop now and get a good look at your mood and your thoughts.

p27.original: 约 翰：（沉默了片刻，然后说）“我告诉自己，他们一点都不尊重人，他们冷漠无情，只在乎自己的利益。他们真是一群混蛋……”
p27.en: Johan: "I was silent for a moment, and then I said, "I told myself that they have no respect for people, they are cold, they care only for their own interests. They're a bunch of assholes...

p28.original: 马歇尔：“谢谢。这足够了。现在你知道自己为什么生气了吗？是因为这些想法吗？”
p28.en: Marshall: "Thank you. That's enough. Now do you know why you're angry? Is that what these ideas are?

p29.original: 约 翰：“但是，这样想有什么不对？”

p30.original: 马歇尔：“我不是说你这样想有什么不对。我也没有说，你不该说他们冷漠无情、自私……。但是，这样的想法让你很生气。想一想，你有什么需要，‘在此时此刻，你需要什么？’”
p30.en: "Marshall: I'm not saying what's wrong with you. Nor did I say that you should not say that they were cold and selfish... But this idea makes you angry. Think, what do you need, "What do you need at this moment?" # # # # # # # I don't know #

p31.original: 约 翰：（沉默了很久，然后说）“马歇尔，我需要他们让我去参加那些培训。如果我无法参加那些培训，出狱后，我还会再进来的。”
p31.en: Johan: (silent for a long time, then) "Marshall, I need them to let me go to those trainings. If I can't attend those trainings, I'll come back after I get out.

p32.original: 马歇尔：“现在你把注意力放在了你的需要上。你是什么样的心情？”
p32.en: Marshall: Now you focus on what you need. What's your mood?

p34.original: 马歇尔：“现在，假定你是监狱的官员，而我是犯人。如果我把你看作是冷漠无情的官僚，即使我没有当面指责你，那样的想法也会通过眼神流露出来。如果我和你说‘我真的很需要那些培训，如果无法接受培训，我担心我迟早还会被送进监狱……’与把你看作是冷漠无情的官僚相比，哪种方式更可能使我的愿望得到满足呢？”
p34.en: Marshall: “Now, assuming you're an officer of the prison, I'm a prisoner. If I see you as a cold-hearted bureaucrat, even if I do not accuse you in person, that idea will be revealed through my eyes. If I said to you, "I really need those trainings, and if I can't, I fear I'll be sent to prison sooner or later..." Which way would my wish be met more than seeing you as a cold-hearted bureaucrat?

p35.original: （约翰眼睛直盯着地板，沉默不语。）
p35.en: John's eyes are on the floor, silent. I don't think so.

p36.original: 马歇尔：“嘿，伙计，在想些什么？”
p36.en: Marshall: "Hey, man, what are you thinking?

p38.original: 三个小时后，约翰过来和我说，“马歇尔，我真希望，你两年前就和我说你早上的那番话，那样，我就不会杀了我最好的朋友。”
p38.en: Three hours later, John came to me and said, “Marshall, I wish you would have told me about your morning speech two years ago, so that I would not have killed my best friend.

p39.original: 如果人们认为自己的痛苦是由其他人造成的，并认为那些人应该受到谴责或惩罚，那么，就像这位年轻的囚犯那样，他们播下了暴力的种子。
p39.en: If people think that their suffering is caused by others and that they deserve to be condemned or punished, then, like the young prisoner, they sow the seeds of violence.

p40.original: 有一次，我发现我的小儿子从他姐姐的房间拿走了五十美分。我问他：“布莱特，你问过姐姐了吗？”“我没有拿她的钱。”他答道。这时，我想到那四种选择。我可以说他撒谎或说他不尊重我，可是指责一个人，往往使我们的愿望更难得到满足。然而，如果我用心体会他的感受和需要，或直接表达我的感受和需要，我的需要就较有可能得到满足。
p40.en: One time, I found my little boy taking 50 cents from his sister's room. I asked him, "Britt, have you asked your sister? "I didn't take her money." He answered. And then I think of those four options. I can say that he lied or that he did not respect me, but that accusing one person often makes it more difficult for us to meet our aspirations. However, my needs are more likely to be met if I feel his feelings and needs, or if I express them directly.

p41.original: 作出选择后，我表达自己的方式，更多的是通过行动而非语言。我倾听他的感受——他感到害怕，他的需要是保护自己避免受到惩罚。通过体会他的感受和需要，我们的感情加深了，这样，我们就能使双方的需要都得到满足。然而，如果在和他说话时，我已经把他看作是不诚实的孩子——不管有没有说出来，他一般就会由于害怕而不敢说出事实。换一句话说，如果把他人看作是说谎的人，那么，这种看法很可能就会成为预言。如果知道说出事实会受到惩罚，为什么还要说出事实呢？
p41.en: After making the choice, I express myself more through action than language. I listened to his feelings — he was afraid, and his need was to protect himself from punishment. By understanding his feelings and needs, our feelings have deepened, so that we can meet the needs of both sides. However, if I had seen him as an dishonest child when I spoke to him — whether or not he had said it, he would have been afraid to tell the truth because he was afraid. In other words, if someone else is seen as a liar, then that perception is likely to become a prophecy. If it is known that it will be punished, why do you have to tell it?

p42.original: 如果我们满脑子是非对错，把某些人看作是贪婪的人、不负责任的人、骗子或其他类型的坏人，那么，我们就很难与他们建立良好的关系。例如，为了保护环境，我们和一个大公司的总经理说：“你知道，你们是名副其实的地球杀手，你们不能再这样滥砍滥伐了！”很明显，以这样的方式去和他们沟通，很难得到积极的回应。在受到指责时，绝大多数的人都无法把注意力放在对方的需要上。当然，指责他人有时可以使我们达到目的——出于害怕、内疚或惭愧，他们改变了自己的行为。
p42.en: It is difficult for us to establish good relations with those who are in our minds and who are seen as greedy, irresponsible, liars or other types of bad people. For example, in order to protect the environment, we said to the general manager of a large company: “You know, you are truly Earth killers, and you can't afford to be so indiscriminate! Clearly, it is difficult to get a positive response to communicate with them in this way. When blamed, the vast majority of people were unable to focus on the needs of the other. Of course, accusing others can sometimes lead us to an end — because they have changed their behaviour out of fear, guilt or shame.

p43.original: 然而，以这样的方式来满足我们的需要，我们也是在使用暴力。为了解决眼前的问题，我们制造了新的问题。批评和指责使人倾向于自我保护并变得更有攻击性。这样，就长期而言，我们给自己增添了更多的麻烦。
p43.en: However, we are also using violence to meet our needs in this way. We have created new problems in order to solve the problems at hand. Criticism and accusations tend to favour self-protection and become more aggressive. In this way, in the long run, we have added more trouble to ourselves.

p45.original: 现在让我们看看非暴力沟通表达愤怒的具体步骤。首先，停下来，除了呼吸，什么都别做。我们避免采取行动去指责或惩罚对方。我们只是静静地体会自己。接着，想一想是什么想法使我们生气了。例如，无意中听到某个人的谈话后，我们认为由于种族的原因自己遭到了排斥。这时，我们体会着愤怒，并留意脑海中盘旋的想法：“这太不公平了！她这是种族歧视！”我们知道，像这样的想法是尚未满足的需要的可悲表达。于是，接下来，就去了解自己想要满足的需要。如果我把某个人当作种族主义者，我的需要也许是接纳、平等、尊重或联系。
p45.en: Let us now look at the concrete steps of Nonviolent Communication expressing anger. First of all, stop. Don't do anything but breathe. We avoid taking action to blame or punish each other. We're just silent about ourselves. Then, think about what's making us angry. For example, after having accidentally heard someone's conversation, we feel that we have been marginalized for reasons of race. At this point, we feel anger and look at the idea of twirling in our minds: "This is so unfair! She's racist! We know that ideas like this are a sad expression of unmet needs. So, then, to understand what you want to meet. If I treat someone as a racist, my need may be to accept, be equal, respect or connect.

p46.original: 为了充分表达自己，我们现在需要张开嘴，说出我们的愤怒——怒火此时已被转化为需要以及与需要相联系的情感。然而，表达此时的感受也许需要很大的勇气。对我来说，生气并冲着人们嚷“你们这是种族歧视”是很容易的。事实上，我甚至还会觉得高兴。但是，倾听心底深处的感受和需要却很可能引发不安。为了充分表达愤怒，我们也许会对那个人说：“你走进房间后，和其他人都打了招呼，却没有和我说话，现在你又在议论白种人，注意到这些，我的胃有些不舒适，而且很害怕，因为我很看重平等。我想请你告诉我，听到我说这些，你的感觉怎么样？”
p46.en: In order to fully express ourselves, we now need to open our mouths and say our anger — anger that has been transformed into need and feelings linked to need at this time. However, it may take a great deal of courage to express what is felt at this time. For me, it is easy to be angry and yell at people that “you are racist”. In fact, I'd even be happy. However, listening to deep-seated feelings and needs is likely to be a source of anxiety. In order to give full expression to our anger, we might say to the man: “You walked into the room, you greeted everyone else, you did not speak to me, and now you talk about the whites, and I noticed that my stomach was a little uncomfortable and scared because I valued equality. I'd like you to tell me, how do you feel when you hear me say this?

p48.original: 然而，在大多数的情况下，在表达自己之前，我们需要先倾听他人。如果对方还处于某种情绪中，他们就很难静下心来体会我们的感受和需要。一旦我们用心倾听他们，并表达我们的理解，在得到倾听和理解之后，他们一般也就会开始留意我们的感受和需要。
p48.en: In most cases, however, we need to listen to others before expressing ourselves. If the other side is still in some mood, it is difficult for them to feel our feelings and needs in peace. Once we listen to them with our heart and express our understanding, they generally also begin to heed our feelings and needs.

p49.original: 有些人，对一些种族和民族，有着某种特定的看法。在过去的30年，我遇到过许多这样的人，并和他们有过交流。有一天清早，我从机场乘出租车前往市区。突然，车内的喇叭传来出租车调度中心的声音：“请到犹太教堂门口接费希曼先生。”接着，坐在我旁边的一位先生嘀咕了一句：“这些该死的犹太人起得这么早，把别人口袋的钱都掏光了。”
p49.en: Some have a particular view of some races and nationalities. Over the past 30 years, I have met many of these people, and I have spoken to them. One morning, I took a taxi from the airport to the city. Suddenly, the sound of the taxi dispatch centre came from the horns inside the car: “Please pick up Mr. Fisherman at the synagogue. Then, a gentleman sitting next to me murmured: “These damn Jews rise so early and have taken all the money out of the other people's bags.

p50.original: 听到这句话后，大约有20秒，我十分恼火。在年轻时，听到这样的话，我的第一反应可能就是揍他一顿。这时，我深呼吸了几次，然后，静静地体会自己的痛苦、恐惧和愤怒。我很在乎自己的感受。我意识到，我生气并不是因为我身边的那位旅客，也不是因为他说的话。虽然他的话激发了我心中的火山，但我知道，我的愤怒和恐惧早已潜伏在那里。我靠后坐了坐，留意那些想伤害他的念头。我甚至想到了他被我狠狠揍了一顿。
p50.en: I'm very upset about that for about 20 seconds. When I was young, my first reaction might have been to beat him up. And then I breathed a few times, and then felt my pain, fear and anger in silence. I care how I feel. I realize that I am not angry because of the passenger I am with, nor because of what he said. Although his words inspired the volcano in my heart, I knew that my anger and fear had already been hidden there. I sat back and looked at the thoughts that were trying to hurt him. I even thought he was beaten up.

p51.original: 这样，我渐渐平静了下来，并开始去体会他的感受和需要。我脱口而出的是：“你感到……？”我试图去了解他的痛苦。为什么？我想了解是什么样的痛苦使他对犹太人如此反感，我还希望他能领会我的感受和需要。我知道，如果他还处于痛苦之中，他就无法倾听我的心声。于是，我想先去了解他，倾听他的心声，并表达我对他的理解和尊重。我过去的经历告诉我，如果我可以理解他，那么，他也就能理解我。这并不容易，但他将能做到这一点。
p51.en: So I gradually calmed down and started to feel his feelings and needs. And what I said out loud was, "Do you feel...? I tried to understand his pain. Why? I want to know what pain is so offensive to the Jews, and I also want him to know what I feel and what I need. I know that if he is still in pain, he cannot listen to my heart. So I want to come to him first, to listen to him, and to express my understanding of and respect for him. My past experience tells me that if I could understand him, then he would understand me. It's not easy, but he'll be able to do it.

p52.original: “你有些不满吧？”我问他，“听起来，你可能有过一些不愉快的经历。”
p52.en: "You're a little upset, aren't you? I asked him, "You may have had some unpleasant experiences.

p53.original: 他看了我一眼。“是的，这些人真惹人讨厌，他们做什么都是为了钱。”
p53.en: He looked at me. “Yes, these people are so annoying, they do everything for money.

p54.original: “你有点厌恶他们，在经济上和他们有来往时，你认为自己需要小心点？”
p54.en: “You're a little sick of them, and you think you need to be careful when you're dealing with them financially?

p55.original: “正是！”他大声说道，接着他就继续表达他的看法。我一边听他讲，一边用心体会他的感受和需要。我意识到，他感到担心，想保护自己。作为一个人，我明白“担心”是怎么一回事，也知道“保护自己”又是多么地重要。当我们专注于他人的感受和需要时，我们就会发现彼此作为人的共同点。虽然，我极不认同他的想法，但我的经历告诉我，如果我不强调我与他人观念的不同，我就较容易接纳他们。特别是当我遇到一个有像他那样想法的人时，倾听他们的感受和需要，而不纠缠于他们的想法，我的生活将会变得愉快得多。
p55.en: "Yes! He spoke out loud, and then he continued to express his views. I listen to him, and I feel his feelings and needs. I realized that he was worried and wanted to protect himself. As a human being, I understand what “fear” is and how important it is to “protect”. When we focus on the feelings and needs of others, we find common ground as human beings. Although I strongly disagree with his ideas, my experience tells me that I would be easier to accept if I did not stress the difference between my perception and that of others. Especially when I meet someone who thinks like him, listening to their feelings and needs, without entangling their thoughts, my life will be much happier.

p56.original: 那位先生一直诉说着他的忧虑和不满。不经意间，他已经从犹太人谈到了黑人。看起来，他渴望有人了解他的痛苦。我静静地听着，大概十分钟后，他停了下来。他觉得我已经理解了他。
p56.en: The same man has been complaining about his anxiety and dissatisfaction. By accident, he had spoken of blacks from Jews. Looks like he wants someone to understand his pain. I listened quietly. About ten minutes later, he stopped. He thinks I understand him.

p57.original: 接下来，我就告诉他我的感受：
p57.en: And then I'll tell him how I feel:

p58.original: 马歇尔：“一开始，听到你对犹太人的评论时，我很生气，也很伤心。因为我对犹太人的印象和你说的很不一样，我真希望你能有一些别的体验。我想请你告诉我，你怎么理解我说的话？”
p58.en: Marshall: At first, when I heard your comments about the Jews, I was angry and sad. Because I have a very different impression of the Jews than you said, and I really hope you have some other experience. I'd like you to tell me how you understand me.

p59.original: 他：“哦，我并没有说他们都是……”
p59.en: He said, "Oh, I didn't say they were all..."

p60.original: 马歇尔：“对不起。我想请你告诉我，你怎么理解我说的话？”
p60.en: Marshall: I'm sorry. I'd like you to tell me how you understand me. I'm sorry.

p61.en: He said, "What are you talking about?

p62.original: 马歇尔：“请让我重复一遍。我真的希望你听到我的痛苦。你听到我的痛苦对我很重要。我刚才说的是，听到你对犹太人的评论，我很伤心。因为我对犹太人的印象和你说的很不一样。我很希望，对犹太人，你能有一些别的体验。我想请你告诉我，你怎么理解我说的话？”
p62.en: Marshall: "Please let me repeat. I really want you to hear my pain. You hear my pain is important to me. I was just saying that I was sad to hear your comments about the Jews. Because I don't feel the same way about Jews. I hope you have some other experience with the Jews. I'd like you to tell me how you understand me.

p63.original: 他：“你的意思是说，我没有权利那样说。”
p63.en: He said, "You mean, I have no right to say that.

p64.original: 马歇尔：“不是这样的。我希望你对我的话有不同的理解。我真的不想指责你。我无意指责你。”
p64.en: Marshall: "That's not true. I hope you understand my words differently. I really don't want to blame you. I have no intention of accusing you.

p65.original: 我试着放慢谈话的节奏。根据我的经验，只要人们认为自己受到了指责，他们就很难体会到别人的痛苦。即使这位先生说“我怎么可以那样说话，我真的太不应该了”，他仍然没有在体会我的痛苦——相反，他沉浸于自我惩罚所带来的痛苦之中。
p65.en: I tried to slow down the conversation. In my experience, it is difficult for them to feel the pain of others as long as they feel that they have been blamed. Even if the gentleman said, “How can I speak like that, I really shouldn't”, he was still not feeling my pain — on the contrary, he was in the pain of self-punitiveness.

p66.original: 我不希望他听到指责，因为我想提醒他我的痛苦。指责别人是很容易的。人们常常觉得自己受到了指责，有时他们自己也同意，并开始恨自己——但这并不意味着他们会改变自己的行为。在另外一些时候，他们痛恨我们称他们为种族主义者或别的——当然，他们也不会改变他们的行为。一旦我们注意到他们认为自己受到了指责，或发现他们在责备自己，我们也许就需要暂时停下来，并去理解他们所经历的痛苦。
p66.en: I do not want him to hear the accusations, because I want to remind him of my pain. It is easy to accuse others. People often feel blamed, sometimes agree with themselves and start hating themselves — but that does not mean that they will change their behaviour. At other times, they hate the fact that we call them racists or something — and, of course, they will not change their behaviour. Once we note that they feel that they have been blamed or that they are blaming themselves, we may need to stop for a while and to understand the suffering they have experienced.

p68.original: 我们需要有足够的耐心来学习和运用非暴力沟通。在与人交往的过程中，我们的第一反应常常是习惯性的反应，因此，运用非暴力沟通有时是很别扭的事。然而，如果我们想要实现自己的人生选择，我们就要给自己充分的时间。
p68.en: We need to be patient enough to learn and use Nonviolent Communication. Our first response in dealing with people is often a customary one, so it is sometimes a strange thing to use Nonviolent Communication. However, if we want to achieve our life choices, we must give ourselves sufficient time.

p69.original: 我的朋友萨姆·威廉斯（Sam Williams）把非暴力沟通的表达形式写在了一张卡片上。每一次老板批评他的时候，他就把卡片掏了出来，提醒自己用非暴力沟通的方式来表达。我问他，老看卡片并花时间组织句子，他的同事是否觉得很奇怪，他回答说：“我并不需要很长的时间来想清楚怎么说，而且，即使时间长了点，我认为也是值得的。对我来说，重要的是，我用自己喜欢的方式来与人联系。”在家里时，他更经常地使用到卡片。他向太太和孩子们解释了为什么他要花时间看卡片。只要一有争论，他就拿出卡片，认真考虑如何以非暴力沟通的方式作出回应。一个月以后，他就不需要再用卡片来提醒自己了。后来，有一天晚上，他和他四岁的孩子在看电视时发生了争执，他的孩子着急了，大声喊道：“爸爸，快拿卡片！”
p69.en: My friend Sam Williams wrote about non-violent forms of communication in a card. Every time the boss criticized him, he pulled out the card, reminding himself to express it in a non-violent way. I asked him if his colleague, who had been looking at the cards and spent time organizing the sentences, had found it strange, and he replied, “I do not need a long time to figure out what to say, and I think it would be worth it even if it had been a little longer. For me, it's important that I communicate with people in the way I like. “When at home, he used the cards more often. He explained to his wife and children why he took the time to watch the cards. Whenever there was a dispute, he would produce a card and seriously consider how to respond by communicating in a non-violent manner. After a month, he doesn't need to remind himself with a card. Then one night, he and his four-year-old boy got into a fight while watching TV, and his kid got anxious and shouted, "Dad, get the card!

p70.original: 如果你希望自己在生气的时候也能运用非暴力沟通，我建议你做以下的练习。在前面，我们已经提到，我们生气是因为我们的想法——我们认为人们“应该”或“不应该”做什么，我们还给人贴上各种标签，并说长论短。请留意我们头脑中“我不喜欢抽烟的人……”之类的想法。然后，问自己：“我不喜欢他们……，是因为我什么样的需要没有得到满足？”通过这样的方式，我们就把注意力放在了尚未得到满足的需要，而不是考虑他人有什么过错。
p70.en: If you wish to use Nonviolent Communication when you are angry, I suggest you do the following exercises. As we have mentioned earlier, we are angry because of our thoughts — what we think people “should” or “should not” do, and we have labels and long-term arguments. Please pay attention to the idea of "I don't like people who smoke" in our minds. And then he asked himself, "I don't like them because what kind of needs I have not met? In this way, we focus on unmet needs rather than on what is wrong with others.

p71.original: 当然，实际运用是至关重要的。大多数人的生活环境和我小时候生活的底特律街区相比，也许会少一些暴力，但也相差不远。在不顺心时，许多人已经习惯于批评和指责他人。因此，在刚开始运用非暴力沟通时，我们可以把节奏放慢些，在说话前先想一想，有时，我们甚至停下来，什么也不说。
p71.en: Of course, practical application is essential. Most people live in conditions that are perhaps less violent than the Detroit neighbourhood where I lived when I was a child, but not far from it. In times of discomfort, many have become accustomed to criticizing and accusing others. So, as we begin to use Nonviolent Communication, we can slow down the pace and think about it before we speak, and sometimes we even stop and say nothing.

p73.original: 在生气时，批评和指责他人都无法真正传达我们的心声。如果想充分表达愤怒，我们就不能归咎于他人，而把注意力放在自己的感受和需要上。与批评和指责他人相比，直接说出我们的需要更有可能使我们的愿望得到满足。
p73.en: When angry, neither criticism nor accusations can truly convey our voices. If we want to fully express our anger, we cannot blame others, but focus on our feelings and needs. It is more likely that our aspirations will be met by speaking directly about our needs than by criticizing and accusing others.

p74.original: 表达愤怒的四个步骤是：（1）停下来，除了呼吸，什么都别做；（2）想一想是什么想法使我们生气了；（3）体会自己的需要；（4）表达感受和尚未满足的需要。有时，在第3步和第4步之间，我们需要先倾听他人。在得到倾听和理解之后，他们也就可以静下心来体会我们的感受和需要。
p74.en: The four steps in expressing anger are: (1) Stop and do nothing but breathe; (2) Think about what makes us angry; (3) To be aware of their own needs; (4) Expressing feelings and unmet needs. Sometimes, between steps 3 and 4, we need to listen to others first. After hearing and understanding, they can also feel our feelings and needs in silence.

p75.original: 我们需要给自己充分的时间来学习和运用非暴力沟通。
p75.en: We need to give ourselves sufficient time to learn and apply Nonviolent Communication.

p77.original: 父亲用非暴力沟通与儿子谈论生死攸关的问题
p77.en: Fathers talk to their sons about life and death with Nonviolent Communication.

p78.original: 15岁的比尔悄悄地把杰克的车开出去兜风，然后又把车完好无损地放回了车库。和比尔一起去兜风的还有杰克14岁的女儿伊娃以及他们的朋友戴维。后来，杰克的女儿把这件事和她父亲说了。接着，比尔的父亲也知道了这件事。以下是比尔和他父亲的对话。
p78.en: The 15-year-old Bill quietly drove Jack's car out for a ride and then put it back in the garage intact. And Jack's 14-year-old daughter Eva and their friend David. Then Jack's daughter told her father about it. And then Bill's father knew about it. Here's the conversation between Bill and his father.

p80.original: 父亲：“我听说，你、伊娃还有戴维，没有和杰克打招呼，就把他的车开走了？”
p80.en: Father: "I heard you, Eva and David took his car without saying hello to Jack?

p81.en: Bill: We didn't drive his car.

p82.original: 父亲：（提高了嗓门）“不要和我撒谎；这对你没什么好处！”（这时，他意识到，为了倾听孩子，他需要先了解自己的感受和需要。）“你坐在那等我一下。我需要好好想想。”（他静下来体会自己。他发现自己又气又怕。他生气是因为他和自己说：“比尔应该懂事点！”“他变成了骗子！”他害怕不仅是因为他想到孩子的行为隐含着危险，而且是因为对孩子缺乏了解也可能带来严重后果。“我真是个笨蛋，居然以为他很懂事！”“万一出事怎么办？”这时，他对自己说：“哦，我需要把‘笨蛋’和‘骗子’这样的标签解读为感受和需要。说自己是‘笨蛋’，我猜我的感受是失望，因为我希望能够信赖自己的判断力。至于‘骗子’，我很害怕，因为我看重诚实与安全。”在沉默中，他考虑如何展开与孩子的对话。）“比尔，你是不是担心，说出事实，你就会受罚？”
p82.en: Father: "Don't lie to me. It won't do you any good! At that point, he realized that in order to listen to children, he needed to know his feelings and needs first. "You sit there and wait for me. I need to think about it. He's quiet and he feels himself. He found himself angry and afraid. He's angry because he said to himself, "Bill should know better!" "He's become a liar!" He fears not only that his child's behaviour is in danger, but also that lack of knowledge of the child may have serious consequences. "I'm such a fool. I can't believe he's so smart! "What if something happens? And then he said to himself, "Oh, I need to read the labels of "wit" and "false" as feelings and needs. I guess I'm disappointed because I want to be able to rely on my judgment. As for the liar, I'm scared because I value honesty and security. In silence, he considered how to engage in dialogue with children. "Bill, are you worried, tell the truth, and you'll be punished?

p83.original: 比尔：“是的。只要我做你不喜欢的事，你就凶得很。”
p83.en: Bill: Yes. As long as I do what you don't like, you're very mean.

p84.original: 父亲：“你的意思是说，你需要理解和尊重？”
p84.en: Father: "You mean, you need to understand and respect?

p85.original: 比尔：“废话！我当然希望你肯理解我、尊重我。”
p85.en: Bill: "Bullshit! I certainly hope that you will understand me and respect me.

p86.original: 父亲：（在心里念叨着：“他这样说话，气死人了！他不知道我正用心和他沟通？他感觉不到我在担惊受怕？现在，我也很需要尊重和体贴。”）“听起来，你很担心，不管你说什么，我都听不进去？”
p86.en: Father: "He talks like this, he's pissed! He doesn't know I'm trying to communicate with him? Can't he feel I'm scared? Now, I also need respect and sensitivity. "Sounds like you're worried. Whatever you say, I can't hear you?

p87.original: 比尔：“你会听吗？一有什么事，你就想动粗。另外，那车的事有什么要紧呢？即使我们真的把车开走了，有人受伤吗？车坏了吗？有什么好大惊小怪的。”
p87.en: Bill: Will you listen? When there's something you want to get rough. Besides, what's so important about the car? Even if we did take the car, did anyone get hurt? Is the car broken? There's nothing to be surprised about.

p88.original: 父亲：“你是担心，如果你承认你开走了车，你的下场会很惨？除非能够信任我，有些话，你就不方便说？”
p88.en: Father: "Are you worried that if you admit that you took the car, you'll be in a terrible situation? Unless you can trust me, you can't say anything?

p90.original: 父亲：（沉默了片刻，给彼此时间体会刚才的对话。）“我怎么做，你才会放心？”
p90.en: Father: (Silence for a moment, give each other time to appreciate the conversation that has just taken place. "What do I do, you don't worry?

p91.original: 比尔：“向我保证，你再也不会惩罚我。”
p91.en: Bill: “Secure me that you will never punish me again.

p92.original: 父亲：（意识到惩罚不仅无法提醒比尔留意他的行为可能的后果，而且还会使父子关系更加疏远，他表示愿意考虑孩子的请求。）“如果你愿意谈下去，我就会考虑你的请求。也就是说，我们继续谈话，直到我能确信你已经意识到你的行为可能会有什么后果。不过，在以后，如果我不清楚你是否已经明白你的行为隐含的危险，我也许会阻止你——但这只是为了保护你。”
p92.en: Father: (Aware that punishment would not only fail to alert Bill to the possible consequences of his behaviour, but would also further alienate paternity, he expressed his willingness to consider the children's request. "If you want to continue, I will consider your request. That is, we will continue to talk until I can be sure that you realize what consequences your actions may have. However, in the future, if I am not sure whether you understand the dangers inherent in your actions, I may have stopped you — but only to protect you.

p93.original: 比尔：“哦，太好了！我这么蠢，为了保护我，你不得不强迫我，呵呵，好极了。”
p93.en: Bill: "Oh, great! I'm so stupid that you had to force me to protect me.

p94.original: 父亲：（与自己的需要失去联系，他对自己说：“我恨不得杀了这小子……他居然这样和我说话！看来，他一点都不在乎我的感受……该死，我现在的需要是什么呢？我这么努力，我是多么需要尊重和体贴啊！”）
p94.en: Father: "I lost touch with my needs, he said to himself, "I hate to kill this kid... He talks to me like this! Looks like he doesn't give a shit about how I feel... shit, what I need right now? I'm trying so hard, how I need respect and kindness! The blogger says:

p95.original: （大声嚷道）“比尔，你知道，你这么和我说话，我烦透了。我耐着性子和你说话，你却那样回答我……你还想和我谈下去吗？”
p95.en: "Bill, you know, you talk to me like that, I'm sick of it. I've been talking to you for a long time, and you've answered me like that... do you want to talk to me?

p97.original: 父亲：“比尔，我真的想听你的心里话。我不想像过去那样指责你、惩罚你。不过，刚才听到你说‘我这么蠢，为了保护我，你不得不强迫我，呵呵，好极了’，我差点就控制不住自己。也许，你愿意帮助我。我的意思是，如果你希望我倾听你，那就请帮助我了解你的想法。如果你不愿意，我只好用老办法来处理这件事情。”
p97.en: Father: "Bill, I really want to hear what you're saying. I don't want to blame you and punish you like I did in the past. But I just heard you say, "I'm so stupid that you have to force me to protect me, huh? Great." I almost couldn't control myself. Maybe you'd like to help me. I mean, if you want me to listen to you, please help me understand your thoughts. If you don't want to, I'll have to deal with it the old way.

p99.original: 父亲：“用老办法，我到这时大概早已告诉你，‘在接下来的两年里，不许你看电视，没有零花钱，不准外出约会，等等’。”
p99.en: Father: "In the old way, I would have told you by the time I got here, "In the next two years, you're not allowed to watch TV, you're not allowed to spend money, you're not allowed to go out on dates, and so on."

p100.original: 比尔：“哦，也许你不妨先试试新办法。”
p100.en: Bill: "Oh, maybe you should try something new first.

p101.original: 父亲：（带点幽默）“很高兴你还有自我保护意识。现在，我想知道，你是否愿意和我坦率地交流，包括你的弱点？”
p101.en: Father: “I'm glad you're still protecting yourself. Now, I wonder if you would be willing to speak frankly to me, including your weaknesses.

p103.original: 父亲：“也就是请你告诉我，对我们说的事情，你是怎样的感受？当然，我也会告诉你我的感受。（坚定的语气）你愿意吗？”
p103.en: Father: "That is to say, how do you feel about what you're saying to us? Of course, I'll tell you how I feel. Would you like that?

p105.original: 父亲：（有点宽慰，叹了一口气）“谢谢。你愿意试一试，我真的很感激。你知道吗？杰克规定，伊娃在三个月内什么活动都不能参加？听到这个消息，你是什么样的感受？”
p105.en: Father: "Thank you. You'd like to try. I really appreciate it. You know what? Jack says Eva can't take part in anything for three months? How do you feel to hear this?

p107.original: 父亲：“我想知道你的感受。”
p107.en: Father: I want to know how you feel.

p108.original: 比尔：“我已经说了，这太不公平了！”
p108.en: Bill: "I've already said, it's not fair!

p109.original: 父亲：（注意到比尔没有提及自己的情感，他决定猜一猜。）“她因为犯错受了这么重的惩罚，你感到难过，是吗？”
p109.en: Father: “Noting that Bill did not mention his emotions, he decided to guess. "You're sorry she's been punished for her sins, aren't you?

p110.original: 比尔：“不，不是这样的。我认为，她根本就没错。”
p110.en: Bill: No, it's not. I think she's absolutely right.

p111.original: 父亲：“她因为响应你的提议受了惩罚，你是不是有些不安？”
p111.en: Father: "Did you feel a little uneasy about her being punished for responding to your offer?

p112.original: 比尔：“是的，是我叫她上车的。”
p112.en: Bill: Yes, I told her to get in the car.

p113.original: 父亲：“看到你的决定对伊娃的影响，你似乎有些伤心？”
p113.en: Father: “Does it seem sad to see how your decision affects Eva?

p115.original: 父亲：“比尔，我真的希望你能意识到你的行为产生的后果。”
p115.en: Father: "Bill, I really want you to be aware of the consequences of your behavior.

p116.original: 比尔：“我当时没有想清楚会有怎样的后果。但我确实把事情搞得一团糟。”
p116.en: Bill: I didn't think clearly about what would happen. But I did make a mess of things.

p117.original: 父亲：“我希望，你注意到你的行为后果不符合你的期待，而不是指责自己。请告诉我，对于把杰克的车开出去兜风这件事，你现在是什么样的感受？”
p117.en: Father: “I hope you notice that the consequences of your actions do not meet your expectations, not blame yourself. Please tell me how you feel about taking Jack's car out for a ride.

p118.original: 比尔：“我觉得我真蠢，爸……我并不想伤害任何人。”
p118.en: Bill: "I think I'm stupid, Dad I don't want to hurt anyone.

p119.original: 父亲：（试图了解比尔的自我评价所反映的感受和需要）“听起来，你很伤心，也很遗憾。因为你需要信任——你无意伤害任何人。”
p119.en: Father: “You sound sad and sorry to hear Bill's self-evaluation of his feelings and needs.” Because you need trust -- you don't mean to hurt anyone. I'm sorry.

p120.original: 比尔：“是的，我并没想到这件事会带来这么大的麻烦。我真的没想到。”
p120.en: Bill: Yeah, I didn't think it would cause so much trouble. I really didn't expect that.

p121.original: 父亲：“你是说，你希望自己在做这件事之前，能够仔细想想可能会有什么后果？”
p121.en: Father: “Are you saying that you want to think about the consequences before you do it?

p122.original: 比尔：（沉默了片刻，体会他父亲说的话。）“我想是的……”
p122.en: Bill: (Silence for a moment, understanding what his father said. “I think so ”

p123.original: 父亲：“现在，我想谈谈我的感受，你开车出去，我怕极了，因为你们的安全对我特别重要。我想请你答应我，熟练掌握车技、拿到驾照以后，再开车出去好吗？”
p123.en: Father: Now, I want to talk about how I feel, and you drive out, and I'm scared, because your safety is of particular importance to me. I'd like you to promise me that you'll drive when you're good at driving and get your license.

p124.original: 比尔：“你这次真的不会惩罚我吗？”
p124.en: Bill: "Are you really not going to punish me this time?"

p125.original: 父亲：“如果你意识到你的行为潜在的危险，并知道保护自己和同伴，我就放心了。为什么要惩罚你呢？”
p125.en: Father: “If you realize the potential danger of your behavior and know to protect yourself and your companions, I am relieved. Why are you being punished?

p126.original: 比尔：“你还会支持我学车吗？”
p126.en: Bill: Will you still support me in driving?

p127.original: 父亲：“当然。我只是希望你熟练掌握车技、拿了驾照，再自己开车去玩。”
p127.en: Father: Of course. I just want you to be good at driving, take your license, and drive yourself.

p128.original: 比尔：“好的。我答应你。实际上，我也知道安全很重要。”
p128.en: Bill: All right. I promise. In fact, I also know that security is important.

p129.original: 父亲：“听你这么说，我很欣慰。你是否愿意告诉杰克你刚才和我说的话？这样，他可能就会放心一些。”
p129.en: Father: I'm glad to hear you say that. Would you like to tell Jack what you just told me? That way, he might feel a little relieved.

p130.original: 比尔：“哦，那太可怕了。他会发疯的。”
p130.en: Bill: "Oh, that's terrible. He'll go crazy.

p131.original: 父亲：“是的，他可能会那样。不过，你愿意为你的行为负责吗？我喜欢杰克，我珍惜我们的友谊，而且，我相信，你也珍惜你和伊娃的友谊，是这样吗？”
p131.en: Father: Yes, he might. But are you willing to take responsibility for your actions? I love Jack, I cherish our friendship, and I believe that you value your friendship with Eva, is that so?

p132.original: 比尔：“她是我最好的朋友之一。”
p132.en: Bill: She's one of my best friends.

p133.original: 父亲：“那我们一起去见他们好吗？”
p133.en: Father, "Shall we go see them together?

p134.original: 比尔：（不太敢去）“哦，那好吧……”

p135.original: 父亲：“你是不是有点害怕？去他家时，你希望能有安全感？”
p135.en: Father, are you a little scared? When you go to his house, you want to feel safe?

p137.original: 父亲：“我们一起去。我会陪伴你、支持你。你愿意去，我真的特别高兴。”
p137.en: Father: "Let's go together. I'll be there for you. I'll be there for you. You're willing to go, I'm really happy.
